qualifying_updates.factual_summary: Meta describes a thin agent orchestrator that separates deterministic workflow phases from model-driven decisions and makes phase transitions explicit.

why_it_matters_for_leaves.docs/wiki/application-patterns/harness-s: Size a harness for explicit phase control and recovery only when the workflow needs it.
why_it_matters_for_leaves.docs/wiki/application-patterns/structure: Make phase outputs reviewable contracts rather than implicit free-form handoffs.
why_it_matters_for_leaves.docs/wiki/application-patterns/user-visi: Emit phase and transition evidence so operators can distinguish deterministic execution from model judgment.
why_it_matters_for_leaves.docs/wiki/governance-and-risk/lifecycle-: Place review gates at consequential phase transitions.
why_it_matters_for_leaves.docs/wiki/source-workflows/raw-project-w: Keep acquisition, qualification, and later synthesis as separately observable phases.

qualifying_updates.follow_up_note: Preserve only the downstream phase-control pattern; route Meta product and platform background upstream.

qualifying_updates.factual_summary: IBM's builder update describes agent identity, remote-MCP integration, guardrails, and evaluation-oriented controls in an orchestration product.

why_it_matters_for_leaves.docs/wiki/governance-and-risk/destructiv: Bind consequential tool authority to a distinct agent identity and reviewable policy.
why_it_matters_for_leaves.docs/wiki/governance-and-risk/governance: Treat identity, scoped remote-tool access, guardrails, and evaluations as a connected control surface.
why_it_matters_for_leaves.docs/wiki/governance-and-risk/prompt-inj: Do not allow untrusted tool or content inputs to silently broaden remote-tool authority.
why_it_matters_for_leaves.docs/wiki/governance-and-risk/prototype-: Require identity, authorization, guardrail, and evaluation evidence before promoting remote-tool workflows.
why_it_matters_for_leaves.docs/wiki/source-workflows/source-reconc: Record product facts as upstream-owned and retain the downstream authorization and evidence implication.
why_it_matters_for_leaves.docs/wiki/coding-practices/layered-ai-co: Use independent reviewers to assess authority boundaries and evidence, not merely generated diffs.

qualifying_updates.follow_up_note: Retain the local control implication only; route IBM, product, and protocol background upstream.

qualifying_updates.factual_summary: OpenAI's October 21 newsroom update describes consistent safeguard expectations across distribution partners and usage-policy enforcement.

why_it_matters_for_leaves.docs/wiki/adoption-and-operating-model/h: Include policy enforcement and evidence collection in total operating cost when selecting execution locations.
why_it_matters_for_leaves.docs/wiki/adoption-and-operating-model/j: Teach operators to recognize policy, authorization, and escalation boundaries before granting autonomy.
why_it_matters_for_leaves.docs/wiki/application-patterns/local-mod: A local runtime does not remove the need to record provider fallback and policy boundaries.
why_it_matters_for_leaves.docs/wiki/source-workflows/public-topic-: Separate public-source collection from policy conclusions and record source/date evidence.
why_it_matters_for_leaves.docs/wiki/governance-and-risk/lifecycle-: Review policy inheritance and enforcement evidence across partner or provider boundaries.
